episodes.name: episode 1
episodes.sequence: upward sequence rising by thirds with apparent cadences on i, III, v

episodes.name: episode 2
episodes.material: end of answer and altered end of CS1; falling steps of CS2 continued by chain of suspensions
episodes.sequence: downward sequence falling by thirds, apparent cadences on i, VI, iv

episodes.name: episode 3
episodes.to_key: ii (with tierce de Picardie, = dominant of v)
episodes.material: new theme in bass, variant of subject notes 5-9, followed in canon at the twelfth by alto; tenor alludes to final figure of subject
episodes.sequence: rising sequence; suggestions of v and VI

episodes.name: episode 4
episodes.material: interchange of episode 3 (alto and soprano), then repeat of episode 2
episodes.sequence: rising, changing at bar 30 to falling

episodes.name: episode 5
episodes.material: subtle variant of episode 2; falling steps of CS2 continued, doubled in tenths, transferred to bass
episodes.sequence: pattern of falling thirds broken: cadence on VI then (not full close) iv

regarded as true perfect cadence (apparent cadences also on i, VI)

cadence on VI then cadence (not full close) on iv

countersubjects.notes: CS1 unchanged at 5-7; CS2 added by tenor at bar 5 with subject's third note; CS2 missing at 7 and 17; [CS2 indicated in brackets at 37-39 in diagram]

subject.answer: subject modulates (first seven notes in i, rest in v); answer drops a tone after the first note and then keeps the subject's intervals, so it is in iv for six notes before returning to i: 'the only possible answer that makes musical sense'

claims.claim: Fugue on a modulating subject, half in g# and half in d#; in 41 bars there are fourteen apparent perfect cadences on i, ii (tierce de Picardie), III, iv, v and VI
The tonal answer drops a tone after the first note and is then in iv for six notes
Episode 1 rises by thirds with apparent cadences on i, III, v; the last is a true cadence
Bass entry at 15 is the subject, not the answer, because of its first note and iv context
Bass entry at 26 in III is the only major-key entry and is harmonized in one key throughout
Tenor entry at 32 sharpens the third degree (b#) and ends without cadential effect
Episode 5 breaks the falling-thirds pattern by a 'bold stroke', cadencing on VI then iv
The coda is 'one of the most effective of all short codas', alluding to episode 1
